source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilient Orange Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 23pp
text:
Because Pursat orange is sensitive to both drought stress and waterlogging, the guide recommends a drip irrigation system (ការគ្រប់គ្រងទឹក, water management) as a climate-resilient way to water orchards. A typical setup includes a raised water tank or reservoir connected through a filter and main pipe to drip lines laid along each planting row, with individual drippers positioned at each tree.

Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone slowly and steadily, which reduces water waste compared to flood or sprinkler irrigation, helps maintain more even soil moisture during dry spells, and lowers the risk of waterlogging since water is not applied faster than the soil can absorb it.
